A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Plasticity as the Mirror of Empowerment. Their main text, equations, figures, notation table, and Appendices A–C are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results, proofs, and conceptual poker and mouse-room examples, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Empirical estimation is proposed as future work.

after.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 3 report original Monte Carlo estimates of plasticity and empowerment for tabular Q-learning on a two-armed Bernoulli bandit.

M1.justification: The proposed GDI, plasticity, and empowerment definitions remain unchanged. The new experiment applies these measures to Q-learning using Monte Carlo estimation; it does not introduce a new proposed learning algorithm or method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds one empirical test scenario: tabular Q-learning interacting with a two-armed Bernoulli bandit. The poker and mouse-room examples were already present as conceptual illustrations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods against a proposed algorithm. Q-learning is the subject of the new sensitivity experiments, not a comparative baseline; the cited empowerment definitions remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: The new bandit study introduces a limited evaluation protocol: Monte Carlo GDI estimation over intervals [1:3] and [2:5], an epsilon sweep from 0 to 1, and an initial-Q sweep from -1 to 1. The second sweep uses initialization-driven exploration without epsilon-greedy exploration.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds two targeted sensitivity analyses testing how exploration probability and optimistic versus pessimistic initialization affect plasticity and empowerment. Figure 3(b) also compares their estimated sum with the theoretical upper bound, within the same toy setting.

E5.justification: Figure 3(a) newly reports mean estimates with bootstrapped confidence intervals; v1 has no empirical uncertainty reporting. The confidence level, bootstrap count, repeated-run count, and seeds are not specified.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds limited empirical findings: plasticity decreases to zero as epsilon reaches 1, optimistic initialization produces higher empowerment than pessimistic initialization, and the estimated sum remains below the plotted bound. These are new toy-experiment results, with no corresponding v1 measurements for direct comparison.

T1.justification: Two existing results receive localized mathematical revisions. Theorem 4.8 changes the bound's interval factors from b-a and d-c to b-a+1 and d-c+1 and revises its upper-bound derivation. Proposition 4.5 and its appendix proof change the Klyubin special case from the full observation sequence O1:n to the terminal observation On.

C1.justification: v2 presents the mirror relationship more explicitly as following from the chosen definitions and singles out the tension theorem as the main result. The discussion replaces the explicit 'first universal definition' novelty claim with 'a general definition of agent plasticity.' The central mirror and tension claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly acknowledges that the framework omits goals and proposes possible reward-focused extensions. Section 4.4 adds interpretations of the exploration and initialization effects, while Section 4.3 explicitly notes that tension may dissipate for nonoverlapping intervals. The deterministic-environment limitation already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: The new experiment discloses tabular Q-learning, a basic Monte Carlo estimator, and execution on a single CPU. Reproducibility information remains limited: neither the main text nor appendices provide a detailed estimator procedure, sample counts, bandit reward probabilities, or implementation access.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wheeler (1910), West-Eberhard (2003), and Ball (2023), connecting behavioral plasticity with biology and discussing goal-directed agency. It removes Jiao et al. (2013) and the associated future-work proposal for GDI estimation. These are focused changes to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion receive targeted rewrites, Section 4.4 is inserted, and the agency conjecture is consolidated into Section 5.4. Section 4.3 is retitled to emphasize the main result. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an additional trade-off diagram, Figure 3 introduces two experimental plots, and Theorem 4.8 receives a box. The existing mouse-room illustration is relocated and renumbered Figure 4; Figure 2 and the notation table retain their display structures.

improvement.justification: The bandit experiments provide limited empirical grounding, the revised figures clarify the central relationship, and the new discussion of omitted goals better qualifies the agency framing. These gains are modest: experimental replication details remain sparse, and Theorem 4.8's interval-length revision is not consistently propagated into its tightness proof, where Equation (100) still uses d-c.
